surface_mechanism_description: The BBr3/H2O precursor system for ALD of B2O3 thin films involves the reaction of BBr3 with surface hydroxyl groups, followed by a water pulse to regenerate OH sites. The high reactivity of B2O3 towards water leads to the formation of volatile boric acid species (H3BO3), which can inhibit film growth at higher temperatures. At lower temperatures, the reaction proceeds through ALD-type growth with a constant growth rate.
evidence: According to the text, 'the initial sequential reactions of B2O3 for the thin film preparation by ALD have been studied, the actual thin films of B2O3 have not been deposited nor their properties reported. Consequently, our interest in B2O3 films stems from the need to exploit the possibilities ALD offers for the processing of binary boron oxide thin films. In this paper, we report the results of boron oxide thin film growth by ALD at low deposition temperatures using BBr3 and H2O as precursors.' Additionally, 'the high reactivity of B2O3 towards water resulting H3BO3 formation' and 'the formation of volatile boric acid species (H3BO3)' are mentioned.
